clue.text: Her tactics confused these designers

indicators.note: confused tells the solver the letters of the preceding words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's muddled tactics baffle a firm of building designers.
explanation.definitionFit: Architects are the professionals who draw up plans for buildings.

clue.text: Delirious about hiking?

definitions.meaning: concerning country walks for pleasure, the pastime of walkers in the countryside

explanation.definitionFit: A delirious person talks disjointedly, and walking for pleasure through the countryside is the same word as a noun.

clue.text: Tool with which man grabs the ring

indicators.note: grabs means one piece takes hold of and encloses another here

parts.note: he is a pronoun standing for a man
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man snatching a ring with some implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled garden implement used for weeding.

clue.text: Pedestrian going right, say, at junction

parts.note: a T-junction gives the letter T

indicators.note: say signals that the word before is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the direction right, pronounced like a ceremony

explanation.surface: A walker turning right at a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like the person on foot, but it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian in the sense of dull and unoriginal is a synonym.

clue.text: Name a girl Heather

parts.note: to name someone is to call them
Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Choosing to christen a baby girl Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather is not the girl's name in the surface but the plant, whose genus is Calluna.
explanation.definitionFit: Calluna is the botanical genus of common heather or ling.

clue.text: Flay the captain — he won't push the boat out!

definitions.text: he won't push the boat out!

parts.note: to flay is to skin
Captain Flint is the pirate captain in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A ship's crew want to whip their captain, who never spends lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: To push the boat out is a British idiom for spending generously on a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is someone who refuses to spend money freely.

clue.text: Mount supplied but may go on foot

definitions.meaning: a backless slipper worn on the foot

explanation.definitionFit: The donkey-horse hybrid is ridden as a mount, and a backless slipper shares the same name.

clue.text: By noon all gum I chewed left my tongue isolated

indicators.note: chewed suggests the letters of the words before are mashed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone chewing gum at midday finds their speech stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking only one language leaves a speaker unable to communicate beyond it.

clue.text: The landlord is a character

definitions.meaning: a written symbol of the alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets out property is literally one who lets, and an alphabetic symbol is the same word.

clue.text: Majestic beard

definitions.meaning: a small pointed tuft on the chin, as worn by Napoleon III

explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means regal or emperor-like, and is also the name of a pointed chin tuft.

clue.text: I get in easily, being light

indicators.note: easily, read loosely, means the letters before move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone slips into a place without trouble because they are slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a description of weight, but it is the verb meaning set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something is to kindle it.

clue.text: Almost all fir found in the mountains

indicators.note: almost means the word that follows loses its final letter

parts.note: a fir is a kind of pine tree

explanation.surface: Fir trees are nearly everywhere up in the high country.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine describes things living or growing high in mountains like the Alps.

clue.text: Foolishly, when in charge, separating fool from friend .

indicators.note: separating means one piece sits between two others, keeping them apart

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone in authority unwisely tries to part a fool from a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a stupid, senseless way is acting foolishly.

clue.text: Misuse of dole fund gradually revealed

indicators.note: misuse suggests the letters of the following words are abused into a new order

explanation.surface: Fraud with unemployment benefit money comes to light bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that unfolds is disclosed step by step.

clue.text: I act in panto? I writhe with apprehension

indicators.note: writhe means the letters twist about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor in a pantomime squirms with stage fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipation is anxious expectation of what is to come.

clue.text: Time a pint is ordered? Can't wait!

indicators.note: is ordered means the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A pub-goer orders a pint and is desperate for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like buying a drink at the bar, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless who cannot bear delay is eager and irritable.

clue.text: Risk I'm prepared to encounter, on the quiet

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made up into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone ready to chance a secret meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encounter' looks like a meeting, but here it means a brief fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter in battle is a minor clash between forces.

clue.text: They provide loads, and drunken trippers tuck in

indicators.note: drunken means the letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: Tipsy day-trippers tuck into food on a coach outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorries with tilting bodies deliver and dump heavy cargoes.

clue.text: Limited edition moribund — not moving with the flow

parts.note: edition cut short gives the abbreviation ed.
moribund means dying

explanation.surface: A collectors' print run is near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Water swirling in a whirlpool runs against the main current rather than with it.

clue.text: Lift in, heave out and thus cause pain

indicators.note: out means the next piece lies outside the other one

parts.note: to heave is to push hard

indicators.note: in a down clue, lift means the word is raised and so reads upwards

explanation.surface: Instructions for hoisting something in and heaving it out, which hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' works only in a down clue, where raising a word makes it read upwards; 'out' here means placed outside, not removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish someone is to inflict suffering as a penalty.

clue.text: Craft due for repair — to be divided in two parts

indicators.note: something sent for repair is fixed up, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A boat awaiting repair is to be split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Furcated means forked, branching into two prongs.

clue.text: Keen to eat eel stew, but vegetarian fare appears

indicators.note: to eat means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: to keen is to wail, to cry

indicators.note: stew means the letters are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner keen on stewed eel is served a vegetable instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager, but it is the verb meaning wail; 'stew' turns EEL into ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a vegetable stalk, food fit for those who eat no meat.

clue.text: He trades in bronco, perhaps ?

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man who deals in wild horses.
explanation.walkthrough: A coper is an old word for a horse dealer, so the bronco suits the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A coper is a dealer, especially in horses.

clue.text: Part of fish that is fisherman's guide

parts.note: a gill is a fish's breathing organ

explanation.surface: A fish's breathing organ described as an angler's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie is a Scottish attendant who guides anglers or deer-stalkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland attendant accompanies those out fishing or shooting.

clue.text: Understood I'm to get it, with central clip readjusted

indicators.note: central means the next piece goes in the middle of the others

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: readjusted means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told they will get it once the middle clip is refitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied though not spoken, so tacitly grasped.

clue.text: The first person to act using international language

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
to act is to do

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to act by speaking an international tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial language derived from Esperanto for world use.

clue.text: Query about the point of having watery milk

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: why is a question
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone asks what use thin milk is.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the thin liquid left after milk curdles.

clue.text: Woolly bears, before taking flight

parts.note: woolly bears are hairy caterpillars; the clue names the winged insects they turn into

explanation.definitionFit: The furry caterpillars called woolly bears develop into these striped insects.
